```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(zoo)
library(sf)
library(here)
library(fixest)
library(did)
library(rdrobust)
library(modelsummary)
library(kableExtra)
library(patchwork)

Proc <- here("data", "processed")

analysis_panel <- readRDS(file.path(Proc, "analysis_panel.rds"))
study_sf       <- readRDS(file.path(Proc, "study_sf.rds"))

study_sf <- study_sf |>
    mutate(london = as.integer(str_starts(ons_code, "E09")))

message("Panel loaded: ", nrow(analysis_panel), " rows | ",
        n_distinct(analysis_panel$ons_code), " study units")
```

```{r}
#| label: prep-estimation
#| message: false

# SCOPE NOTE. panel_est is filtered to 2019 Q1 onward, and post_announce /
# t_announce are defined relative to the 2023 announcement (2022 Q4). The TWFE,
# event study and RDD specifications built on this object therefore speak to
# the 2023 wave only — the 2019 announcement (2017 Q2) and the 2021
# confirmation (2018 Q2) both fall outside or at the very edge of this window.
# The spillover and pre-2023 trajectory plots below use the full panel and do
# cover the earlier waves.
panel_est <- analysis_panel |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    mutate(
        london          = as.integer(str_starts(ons_code, "E09")),
        borough_id      = as.integer(factor(ons_code)),
        time_id         = as.integer(factor(yq)),
        period          = year * 4 + quarter,
        log_ulev_share  = log(ulev_share + 0.0001),
        log_house_price = log(house_price)
    ) |>
    filter(yq >= as.yearqtr("2019 Q1"))

message("Estimation sample: ", nrow(panel_est), " rows")
message("  London boroughs: ", n_distinct(panel_est$ons_code[panel_est$london == 1]))
message("  Surrounding districts: ", n_distinct(panel_est$ons_code[panel_est$london == 0]))
message("  Quarters: ", n_distinct(panel_est$yq))
```

```{r}
#| label: twfe-did
#| message: false

# =============================================================================
# TWFE DiD specifications — 2023 wave (no additional covariates)
# Treated = outer London boroughs (london == 1, treated == 1)
#
# NOTE ON THE CONTROL GROUP. The "London only" specifications use inner London
# boroughs as controls. Those boroughs were themselves treated in 2019 and
# 2021, so this is precisely the already-treated-as-control comparison that
# Goodman-Bacon (2021) shows can be biased under heterogeneous or dynamic
# treatment effects. It is retained deliberately as the naive benchmark: the
# contrast with the specifications that add never-treated surrounding
# districts shows empirically how much the comparison group matters, which is
# the Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) point. The surrounding-district
# specifications, not the London-only ones, are the preferred estimates.
# =============================================================================

# 1. Naive baseline — London only (inner London as control: biased benchmark)
twfe_base <- feols(
    ulev_share ~ treated:post_announce |
        borough_id + time_id,
    data    = panel_est |> filter(london == 1),
    cluster = ~ons_code
)

# 2. With surrounding districts as additional never-treated controls
twfe_surround <- feols(
    ulev_share ~ treated:post_announce |
        borough_id + time_id,
    data    = panel_est |>
        filter(treated == 1 | london == 0),
    cluster = ~ons_code
)

# 3. With linear trends — London only
twfe_trends <- feols(
    ulev_share ~ treated:post_announce + treated:t_announce |
        borough_id + time_id,
    data    = panel_est |> filter(treated == 1 | london == 0),
    cluster = ~ons_code
)

# 4. With linear trends — including surrounding districts
twfe_trends_surround <- feols(
    ulev_share ~ treated:post_announce + treated:t_announce |
        borough_id + time_id,
    data    = panel_est,
    cluster = ~ons_code
)

saveRDS(list(naive = twfe_base, preferred = twfe_surround,
             naive_trends = twfe_trends, preferred_trends = twfe_trends_surround),
        file.path(out, "twfe_models.rds"))                  # SECTION 6

modelsummary(
    list(
        "Naive\n(London only)"           = twfe_base,
        "Preferred\n(+ Surrounding)"     = twfe_surround,
        "Naive + Trends\n(London only)"  = twfe_trends,
        "Preferred + Trends"             = twfe_trends_surround
    ),
    stars   = c("*" = 0.1, "**" = 0.05, "***" = 0.01),
    gof_map = c("nobs", "adj.r.squared", "rmse"),
    title   = "TWFE DiD: ULEV Compliance Share (no covariates)"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: event-study
#| message: false

panel_est <- panel_est |>
    mutate(
        t_bin = case_when(
            t_announce < -12 ~ -12L,
            t_announce > 6   ~  6L,
            TRUE             ~ as.integer(t_announce)
        ),
        t_bin = relevel(factor(t_bin), ref = "-1")
    )

# Event study — London only
es_london <- feols(
    ulev_share ~ i(t_bin, treated, ref = c("-1", "-12")) + log_house_price |
        borough_id + time_id,
    data    = panel_est |> filter(london == 1),
    cluster = ~ons_code
)

# Event study — including surrounding districts
es_surround <- feols(
    ulev_share ~ i(t_bin, treated, ref = c("-1", "-12")) + log_house_price |
        borough_id + time_id,
    data    = panel_est |> filter(treated == 1 | london == 0),
    cluster = ~ons_code
)

# Extract and plot
extract_es <- function(model, label) {
    broom::tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE) |>
        filter(str_detect(term, "t_bin")) |>
        mutate(t = as.integer(str_extract(term, "-?\\d+")),
               spec = label) |>
        bind_rows(tibble(
            term = c("ref_-1", "ref_-12"),
            estimate = 0, std.error = 0,
            conf.low = 0, conf.high = 0,
            t = c(-1L, -12L), spec = label
        )) |>
        arrange(t)
}

es_coefs <- bind_rows(
    extract_es(es_london,   "London only"),
    extract_es(es_surround, "With surrounding districts")
)

p_event_study <- ggplot(es_coefs, aes(x = t, y = estimate, colour = spec, fill = spec)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = -0.5, linetype = "dotted", colour = "black") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 2.5,  linetype = "dotted", colour = "red") +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = 0.15,
                colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    annotate("text", x = -0.5, y = Inf, vjust = 2, hjust = -0.1,
             label = "Announcement", size = 3, colour = "black") +
    annotate("text", x = 2.5, y = Inf, vjust = 2, hjust = -0.1,
             label = "Implementation", size = 3, colour = "red") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(
        "London only"                  = "steelblue",
        "With surrounding districts"   = "firebrick"
    )) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(
        "London only"                  = "steelblue",
        "With surrounding districts"   = "firebrick"
    )) +
    labs(
        title    = "Event Study: ULEV Compliance Share",
        subtitle = "Treated = outer London boroughs | Reference period = t−1",
        x        = "Quarters relative to announcement (2022 Q4 = 0)",
        y        = "Estimated coefficient",
        colour   = NULL, fill = NULL,
        caption  = "SEs clustered by borough. Borough and quarter FE. Control: log house price."
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")

ggsave(file.path(figs, "event_study.png"), p_event_study,
       width = 7, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)   # SECTION 6

p_event_study
```

```{r}
#| label: its
#| message: false

# =============================================================================
# Interrupted Time Series (ITS)
# Tests whether announcement caused level shift or trend change
# Three groups: inner London, outer London, surrounding districts
# =============================================================================

its_data <- analysis_panel |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    mutate(
        group = case_when(
            london == 1 & treated == 0 ~ "Inner London (Control)",
            london == 1 & treated == 1 ~ "Outer London (Treated)",
            london == 0                ~ "Surrounding Districts"
        ),
        t = as.numeric(yq) - min(as.numeric(yq)),
        time_since_announce = pmax(0, as.numeric(yq) - 
                                   as.numeric(as.yearqtr("2022 Q4")))
    ) |>
    group_by(yq, group, t, time_since_announce, post_announce) |>
    summarise(
        mean_ulev_share = mean(ulev_share, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
    )

# Run ITS for each group
its_inner <- lm(
    mean_ulev_share ~ t + post_announce + time_since_announce,
    data = its_data |> filter(group == "Inner London (Control)")
)

its_outer <- lm(
    mean_ulev_share ~ t + post_announce + time_since_announce,
    data = its_data |> filter(group == "Outer London (Treated)")
)

its_surrounding <- lm(
    mean_ulev_share ~ t + post_announce + time_since_announce,
    data = its_data |> filter(group == "Surrounding Districts")
)

saveRDS(list(inner = its_inner, outer = its_outer,
             surrounding = its_surrounding),
        file.path(out, "its_models.rds"))                   # APPENDIX

modelsummary(
    list(
        "Inner London (Control)" = its_inner,
        "Outer London (Treated)" = its_outer,
        "Surrounding Districts"  = its_surrounding
    ),
    stars   = c("*" = 0.1, "**" = 0.05, "***" = 0.01),
    gof_map = c("nobs", "adj.r.squared", "rmse"),
    title   = "Interrupted Time Series Results by Group"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: its-did
#| message: false

# DiD-ITS — outer London vs surrounding districts only
# Surrounding districts = baseline (never-treated)
# This isolates the announcement effect specific to outer London
# above the common trend in surrounding districts

its_did_data <- analysis_panel |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    filter(london == 1 & treated == 1 | london == 0) |>
    mutate(
        t = as.numeric(yq) - min(as.numeric(yq)),
        time_since_announce = pmax(0, as.numeric(yq) -
                                   as.numeric(as.yearqtr("2022 Q4")))
    ) |>
    group_by(yq, treated, london, t, time_since_announce, post_announce) |>
    summarise(
        mean_ulev_share = mean(ulev_share, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(
        outer_london = as.integer(london == 1 & treated == 1)
    )

its_did_model <- lm(
    mean_ulev_share ~ t + outer_london +
        post_announce + post_announce:outer_london +
        time_since_announce + time_since_announce:outer_london,
    data = its_did_data
)

saveRDS(its_did_model, file.path(out, "its_did_model.rds"))  # SECTION 6

summary(its_did_model)
```

```{r}
#| label: spillover-test
#| message: false

# Test for spillover effects from earlier expansions
# If surrounding districts accelerated ULEV adoption after 2019 and 2021
# expansions despite never being subject to ULEZ, that's spillover evidence

spillover_data <- analysis_panel |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    mutate(
        group = case_when(
            london == 1 & treated == 0 ~ "Inner London (Control)",
            london == 1 & treated == 1 ~ "Outer London (Treated)",
            london == 0                ~ "Surrounding Districts (Never-Treated)"
        )
    ) |>
    group_by(yq, group) |>
    summarise(
        mean_ulev_share = mean(ulev_share, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
    )

p_spillover <- ggplot(spillover_data, aes(x = yq, y = mean_ulev_share, colour = group)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    # 2019 expansion — announcement 2017 Q2 (4 April 2017 mayoral proposal)
    # CHANGED: was 2017 Q1, which predates the announcement and did not match
    # the synthetic control specification (i_time = 2017.25).
    geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(as.yearqtr("2017 Q2")),
               linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(as.yearqtr("2019 Q2")),
               linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.5) +
    # 2021 expansion — announcement 2018 Q2 (8 June 2018 TfL confirmation)
    # CHANGED: was 2019 Q2, a specification since abandoned in favour of the
    # formal confirmation date (i_time = 2018.25).
    geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(as.yearqtr("2018 Q2")),
               linetype = "dashed", colour = "purple", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(as.yearqtr("2021 Q4")),
               linetype = "dotted", colour = "purple", linewidth = 0.5) +
    # 2023 expansion
    geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(as.yearqtr("2022 Q4")),
               linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(as.yearqtr("2023 Q3")),
               linetype = "dashed", colour = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
    annotate("text", x = as.numeric(as.yearqtr("2017 Q2")),
             y = Inf, vjust = 1.5, hjust = -0.1, size = 2.5,
             label = "2019\nAnn.", colour = "grey40") +
    annotate("text", x = as.numeric(as.yearqtr("2018 Q2")),
             y = Inf, vjust = 1.5, hjust = -0.1, size = 2.5,
             label = "2021\nAnn.", colour = "purple") +
    annotate("text", x = as.numeric(as.yearqtr("2022 Q4")),
             y = Inf, vjust = 1.5, hjust = -0.1, size = 2.5,
             label = "2023\nAnn.", colour = "black") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(
        "Inner London (Control)"              = "steelblue",
        "Outer London (Treated)"              = "firebrick",
        "Surrounding Districts (Never-Treated)" = "darkgreen"
    )) +
    labs(
        title    = "ULEV Adoption Trajectories — Spillover Test",
        subtitle = "All three ULEZ expansion announcements and implementations",
        x        = "Quarter",
        y        = "Mean ULEV share",
        colour   = NULL,
        caption  = "Dashed = announcement. Dotted = implementation."
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")

ggsave(file.path(figs, "spillover.png"), p_spillover,
       width = 7, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)   # SECTION 6
```

```{r}
#| label: rdd
#| message: false

# =============================================================================
# FEASIBILITY ASSESSMENT — geographic regression discontinuity
#
# This section establishes that a geographic RD design cannot be credibly
# identified at borough level, and is therefore reported as a feasibility
# assessment rather than as a robustness check. Two obstacles, the second
# binding.
#
# (1) Coincident treatment. The 2023 expansion boundary is the Greater London
#     boundary, but the available borough-level running variables measure
#     distance to the 2019 and 2021 boundaries. Both coincide with earlier ULEZ
#     treatment: units inside the 2021 boundary had been subject to enforcement
#     since October 2021, while units outside were not yet covered for cars.
#     A discontinuity at rv_2021 = 0 during the 2023 anticipation window
#     therefore mixes the accumulated effect of the 2021 expansion with any
#     anticipatory response to 2023, violating the no-coincident-treatments
#     condition set out by Keele and Titiunik (2015).
#
# (2) Density at the cutoff. Geographic RD compares observations immediately
#     either side of a border and so requires many units near it. Each borough
#     contributes a single observation at a single distance, so within any
#     plausible bandwidth only a handful of units remain on each side. This
#     constraint follows from the level of spatial aggregation and would apply
#     to any choice of boundary, including a correctly specified Greater London
#     running variable. The diagnostic below establishes the magnitude.
#
# Estimates are retained for transparency but are not interpretable as causal.
# =============================================================================

# --- Density diagnostic: how many boroughs sit near the boundary at all? ---
rdd_density <- panel_est |>
    filter(yq == as.yearqtr("2022 Q4"), london == 1, !is.na(rv_2021)) |>
    mutate(
        band = case_when(
            abs(rv_2021) <= 2 ~ "Within 2km",
            abs(rv_2021) <= 5 ~ "2-5km",
            TRUE              ~ "Beyond 5km"
        ),
        side = if_else(rv_2021 < 0, "Inside 2021 zone", "Outside 2021 zone")
    ) |>
    count(band, side) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = side, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

saveRDS(rdd_density, file.path(out, "rdd_density.rds"))      # SECTION 6

rdd_density |>
    kable(
        caption = "Borough Density by Distance Band from the 2021 Boundary (2022 Q4)"
    ) |>
    kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"))

rdd_dates <- list(
    pre_announce  = as.yearqtr("2022 Q3"),
    announcement  = as.yearqtr("2022 Q4"),
    anticipate_1  = as.yearqtr("2023 Q1"),
    anticipate_2  = as.yearqtr("2023 Q2"),
    implement     = as.yearqtr("2023 Q3"),
    post_1        = as.yearqtr("2023 Q4")
)

rdd_results <- map(rdd_dates, function(target_yq) {
    cs <- panel_est |>
        filter(yq == target_yq,
               london == 1,
               !is.na(rv_2021),
               !is.na(ulev_share))
    rdrobust(y = cs$ulev_share, x = cs$rv_2021,
             c = 0, p = 1, kernel = "triangular")
})

# Extract results
rdd_table <- map_dfr(names(rdd_results), function(name) {
    res <- rdd_results[[name]]
    tibble(
        period    = name,
        estimate  = round(res$coef[2], 5),
        se        = round(res$se[2], 5),
        pvalue    = round(res$pv[2], 4),
        bw_km     = round(res$bws[1], 2),
        n_left    = res$N[1],
        n_right   = res$N[2]
    )
})

saveRDS(rdd_table, file.path(out, "rdd_table.rds"))          # APPENDIX

rdd_table |>
    select(period, n_left, n_right, bw_km, estimate, se, pvalue) |>
    kable(
        caption   = paste("Illustrative RD Estimates at the 2021 Boundary.",
                          "Reported for transparency only: the effective",
                          "sample sizes below are too small, and the boundary",
                          "coincides with earlier treatment, so these are not",
                          "interpretable as causal estimates."),
        col.names = c("Period", "N (inside)", "N (outside)", "Bandwidth (km)",
                      "Estimate", "SE", "p-value")
    ) |>
    kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"))
```

```{r}
#| label: rdd-note
#| message: false

# Which boroughs actually fall inside the data-driven optimal bandwidth?
# Naming them makes the identification problem concrete: the estimate rests
# on these units alone.
#
# CHANGED: bandwidth was hardcoded at 2.24km from an earlier run. It is now
# read from the fitted object so it cannot fall out of step if the RDD is
# re-estimated.
bw_announce <- rdd_results$announcement$bws[1]

message("Optimal bandwidth at announcement: ", round(bw_announce, 2), "km")

panel_est |>
    filter(yq == as.yearqtr("2022 Q4"), london == 1) |>
    mutate(in_bw = abs(rv_2021) <= bw_announce) |>
    group_by(in_bw, treated) |>
    summarise(
        n        = n(),
        boroughs = paste(la_name, collapse = ", "),
        .groups  = "drop"
    ) |>
    kable(
        caption   = paste0("Boroughs Within Optimal Bandwidth (",
                           round(bw_announce, 2), "km)"),
        col.names = c("Within BW", "Treated", "N", "Boroughs")
    ) |>
    kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"))
```
